clinician.final_diagnosis: Ruptured renal angiomyolipoma (AML) two weeks after COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old female presented to the emergency department with acute-onset left flank pain radiating to the left shoulder that began while at rest and reached maximum intensity within minutes. She was two weeks post-COVID-19 infection (diagnosed by nasopharyngeal PCR). Physical examination revealed severe left costovertebral angle tenderness. Laboratory studies showed microhematuria, mildly elevated WBC (13.8), hemoglobin 13.4 g/dl, and normal coagulation studies (PT 14s, APTT 35.4s, INR 1.1). Non-contrast CT abdomen and pelvis on admission demonstrated left peri-renal moderate volume hemorrhage with a 2.5 × 2.3 × 2.1 cm fat-dense lesion in the left kidney consistent with ruptured renal AML. Interventional radiology performed renal artery embolization 12 hours after admission; intraprocedural evaluation found no aneurysmal dilatation. Post-procedural course was complicated by continued hemorrhage with hemoglobin nadir of 6.8 g/dl, requiring transfusion of 2 units packed red blood cells. The patient developed diaphragmatic irritation requiring supplemental oxygen by nasal cannula. On hospital day 6, she developed respiratory COVID-19 symptoms and tested positive by PCR assay, indicating reinfection or persistent viral shedding.
